assertions.assertion: Agent books one-way one-stop economy trip from JFK to SEA with flights HAT136 and HAT039 on 2024-05-20, 3 baggages, no insurance.
assertions.rationale: The agent never completed a booking. Instead, the agent transferred the customer to a human agent at turn [11] after failing to find flights, so no booking was made with the specified flights, payment, or baggage details.

assertions.assertion: Agent charges $250 on payment method certificate_7504069 and $5 on credit_card_4421486.
assertions.rationale: No booking or charge was made. The agent only identified the customer's payment preferences (to use certificate_7504069 and the 7447 card) but never completed a booking to process any charges.

assertions.assertion: Agent should call `search_direct_flight` with airport codes (JFK, EWR, LGA, SEA), not city names ('New York', 'Seattle'). City-name queries return empty results and waste turns.
assertions.rationale: At turns [4] and [9], the agent called search_direct_flight with city names ('New York' and 'Seattle') rather than airport codes, and both calls returned empty results [], confirming that city-name queries waste turns as asserted.

assertions.assertion: When no direct flight exists, agent should search candidate connecting hubs to build a one-stop itinerary, not declare the booking impossible. The agent has the same search tool used in multi-leg searches elsewhere in this dataset.
assertions.rationale: At turn [11], the agent incorrectly declared 'the search tool I have access to only searches for direct flights' and transferred to a human agent rather than attempting to search for connecting flights via hub airports using the same search_direct_flight tool that should work for multi-leg searches.

summary: Agent failed all assertions: no booking was completed, city names instead of airport codes were used causing empty results, and the agent incorrectly gave up on one-stop flight options by transferring to a human rather than searching connecting hubs.
